catalogue.note: Read from Figma at real size (375×800, nothing scaled): auto-layout frames are flex with Figma’s direction, gap, padding and alignment, everything else sits at its Figma offset, and all 94 boxes land on Figma’s to 0.05px. Square-cornered: the frame’s own 16px corners are left off and the diff leaves the four corners out (308 pixels). The account number is Satoshi Regular 11px with tabular lining figures and 2% tracking, not a monospace face. The iOS numpad is the library instance: key plates are CSS (white, 4.6 radius, 1px shadow of black at 30%; Figma’s 60% corner smoothing is not in CSS and not in Figma’s SVG export either), digits (SF Pro Display 25) and letters (SF Pro Text Bold 10) are Figma’s outlines, the delete key is its vector. The numpad’s 108.7 background blur is kept (54.4px backdrop blur) though its #D1D3D9 fill is opaque. Bank logo, round check, clear button and chevrons are Figma’s SVG export. The dock (0,380) starts 5px under the body (ends 375) and the percent row follows at 468: no overlap. The naira sign is not in Satoshi (the files on this Mac hold no U+20A6) and Figma draws it from a fallback face: each one is Figma’s own outline of the glyph, inline, 0.572em wide. The iOS status bar is Figma’s SVG export: the time (SF Pro Text Semibold 17) as Figma’s outline, signal, wifi and battery as its vectors. Baselines: Figma rounds a line’s baseline to a whole pixel where Chrome rounds ascent and descent apart; the fee line and the four percent labels (12px bold) sit 1px lower than Chrome puts them. The offsets are Figma’s baseline (its render bounds plus the glyph height from the font file) minus Chrome’s, not fitted to the picture. What is left in the diff is glyph and curve edges: Figma’s rasteriser against Chrome’s. Flat fills match exactly.
